notes:
Account snapshot: Lighthouse LLM Fabric builds predictive routing and ETA services for last-mile logistics; latency at edge is business-critical. They ingest telemetry from 200k vehicles and need LLM inference to run in the decision loop for route re-ranking and driver assist chat. Strong preference for deterministic tail latency and predictable unit cost. Interested in Redwood for unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private with clear cost/perf tradeoffs.

Sales/Eng summary (shorthand):
- 2026-01-15 discovery call (Avery/Ravi) — customer: "we need sub-50ms p95 on short prompts; p99 target <120ms for reranking". Wants cost < $0.0008/token equivalent when amortized across throughput.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML + KMS for key management, retention controls and audit logs mandatory. Data residency: US-only.
- Preference: open-source models quantized to int8/int4 if quality OK; fallback routing to larger model for ambiguous queries.
- Performance levers they're most interested in: batching (dynamic batching w/ tail SLOs), KV/prefix caching for repeated context, model quantization profiles and kernel selection. Also want perf benchmark harness they can run in-house.
- POC approach agreed: Redwood to run a 48-hour perf sweep on dedicated pool + provide a self-contained benchmarking script for on-prem team. Benchmarks required: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint, cost-per-token estimates across quantization profiles and batch sizes.
- Quote request: include two configs — 1) Dedicated small cluster (N=4 A10s equivalent) with autoscale burst, 2) Private on-prem package with SRE playbook + air-gapped deploy checklist.

Customer quotes/snippets:
- "We can't afford jitter on peak hours — rerank mustn't exceed 150ms p99 or we lose SLAs to carriers."
- "Show me explicit cost math comparing dynamic batching vs static micro-batching across 1M requests/day."
